definition: A psychological network is a way of mapping psychosocial factors and the links among them so researchers can examine how those factors relate to a particular behavior or outcome. In this source, it is used to study factors connected with children’s football participation.

reasons: The packet supports that psychological network analysis was used to examine selected psychosocial factors related to football participation among primary school students, but it does not define a psychological network as a general way of mapping factors and their links.

The definition adds a broader claim about examining how factors relate to any particular behavior or outcome, which is not stated in the packet and goes beyond the source’s specific use in this article.
The packet does not explicitly define a “psychological network” as a “way of mapping psychosocial factors and the links among them,” nor does it explicitly describe the mapping/link mechanism.

The packet mentions that the study “utilized psychological network analysis to examine selected psychosocial factors related to football participation,” but it does not support the broader phrasing that the purpose is “so researchers can examine how those factors relate to a particular behavior or outcome.”

The claim that “In this source, it is used to study factors connected with children’s football participation” is broadly consistent with the packet, but it is not enough to rescue the unsupported generalizations in the first sentence.
